Chapter Ten: The Mind of the Tathāgata, from the "Appearance of the Tathāgata" Section.
O Sons of the Buddha, the wisdom of the Tathāgata reaches everywhere. Why is this? Because there is not a single sentient being who does not possess the wisdom of the Tathāgata;
it is only because of delusive thoughts, inversions, and attachments that they do not realize it. If one is free from such delusions...
When one contemplates, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā*), the self-existent knowledge (*svayambhūjñāna*), and the unimpeded knowledge (*asaṅgajñāna*) will then manifest before one.
Son of the Buddha, it is like a great scripture whose size is equal to a trichiliocosm, upon which are inscribed all the events within that trichiliocosm.
All [of these] would be exhausted. That is to say: writing down the events within the Great Iron Ring Mountains (Mahācakravāḍa), the volume would equal the Great Iron Ring Mountains;
writing down the events within the great earth, the volume would equal the great earth; writing down the events within a medium chiliocosm, the volume would equal a medium chiliocosm;
writing down the events within a small chiliocosm, the volume would equal a small chiliocosm. Thus it is.
Whether it be the four continents, the great oceans, Mount Sumeru, the palaces of the terrestrial devas, the palaces of the space-dwelling devas of the desire realm,
the palaces of the form realm, or the palaces of the formless realm— if each were transcribed, their dimensions would all be equal.
Although this great scripture is equal in size to a trichiliocosm, it remains entirely contained within a single location.
Within a single atom, as it is with one atom, so it is with all atoms.
At that time, there was a person of clear and penetrating wisdom who possessed the fully perfected, pure divine eye.
Seeing this sutra scroll within the atom, he perceived that it provided no benefit whatsoever to sentient beings. He then thought: "I shall, by the power of diligence, shatter that atom."

Having thought, "I shall bring forth this sutra scroll from within these atoms so as to benefit all sentient beings," he immediately employs skillful means to break open those atoms and bring forth this sutra scroll, thereby causing all sentient beings to universally obtain benefit.
As it is with one atom, so it should be known that it is likewise for all atoms. Son of the Buddha, the wisdom of the Tathāgata is also like this, without...
Its measure is unimpeded, universally able to benefit all sentient beings, and it is fully present within the bodies of all beings.
Yet, because ordinary, ignorant people are attached through their deluded imaginings, they neither know nor perceive it, and thus fail to obtain its benefits.
At that time, the Tathāgata, with his unobstructed and pure eye of wisdom, surveyed all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm and spoke these words: "How marvelous!"
How marvelous! How extraordinary! These sentient beings possess the wisdom of the Tathāgata, yet they are deluded by ignorance and fail to know or see it.

I shall instruct them in the Noble Path so that they may forever abandon their false conceptions and attachments, and perceive within their own bodies the vast wisdom of the Tathāgata, which is no different from that of the Buddha. Thus, I shall teach those sentient beings to practice.

The Noble Path causes one to be free from false conceptualization. Having become free from false conceptualization, one realizes the immeasurable wisdom of the Tathāgata, thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha, this is the tenth characteristic of the Tathāgata’s mind;
all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas should understand it in this way.

In the *Xitang Zalu*, it is recorded that during the Yuanyou era, there was a monk from Shu named Dharma Master Zhichao who had been constantly reciting the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* for thirty years.
One day, he happened to see a young boy with a refined and clear countenance who raised his hand in a formal salutation. Zhichao said:

"Where have you come from? he asked. "From Mount Wutai," the man replied. Chao said, "How have you traveled so far to reach here? He replied, "I have a small matter by which I wish to instruct you. Chao said, "I wish to hear it.
The man said, "It is truly praiseworthy that our Master recites the sutras; however, his error lies in the matter of cleaning himself after using the toilet.
When washing, he touches water that drenches the back of his hand, yet he never uses ash or clay to wash it (or alternatively, soap-nut balls may also be used). So it was said.
The use of ash for hand-washing was prescribed by the Vinaya in seven applications; nowadays, however, it is done only two or three times.

Because of this, the residual defilement still remains, such that even performing prostrations to the Buddha or reciting the sutras incurs offense. Having said this, [the apparition] vanished. Daochao felt ashamed and reformed his ways.

A Warning Text for Reading Sutras (Composed by Chan Master Baoning Yong) Regarding the method of reading sutras, those who are new to the study must know this:
one should purify the three karmas. If the three karmas are without deficiency, then a hundred blessings will gather together.
The three karmas are those of body, speech, and mind. First, sit upright with the body composed, as if facing the countenances of the sages. Then...
First, the physical karma is purified. Second, the mouth is free from frivolous speech and all jesting is severed; thus, the verbal karma is purified.
Third, the mind is not distracted and all external conditions are stilled; thus, the mental karma is purified. Once the inner mind is tranquil, external objects are all relinquished.

Only then can one accord with and awaken to the true source; only then may one hope to investigate and exhaustively master the principles of the Dharma. This may be likened to water becoming clear so that pearls shine within it, or clouds dispersing so that the moon is bright.
The ocean of meaning surges from within the breast, and the mountain of wisdom gathers before the ears and eyes. Such a task must not be undertaken lightly; it is truly no small matter.
When both mind and dharmas are forgotten, and both self and others are benefited—if one can act thus, this is truly repaying the Buddha’s kindness.

"Faith gives birth to the Buddha-family" (Qingliang says: "Cultivation through effort will ultimately result in ruin after many kalpas; when the essence of the mindless state reaches its ultimate limit, one suddenly accords with the Buddha-family in a single thought-moment").
The *Tathāgatotpattisambhava-parivarta* states: "O Son of the Buddha, this Dharma-gate is not taught by the Tathāgata for other sentient beings;
it is taught only for Bodhisattvas who are heading toward the Mahāyāna, and only for Bodhisattvas who ride the inconceivable vehicle. This Dharma..."
This gate does not fall into the hands of any other sentient beings, with the sole exception of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha, it is like the seven treasures possessed by a Cakravartin King; because of these treasures, he is manifested as a Wheel-Turning King.
These treasures do not fall into the hands of other sentient beings, except for the crown prince born of the first queen, who is fully accomplished in holiness.

Regarding the regent of the king: if a Wheel-Turning King has no such crown prince endowed with all virtues, then after the king’s death, these various jewels will all vanish and perish within seven days.
Son of the Buddha, this treasure of the sutra is likewise;
it does not fall into the hands of any other sentient beings, except for the true sons of the Tathāgata, the Dharma King, who are born from the Tathāgata.
The Family: Those who plant the various roots of goodness that constitute the marks of a Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha, if there were no such true sons of the Buddha, this Dharma-gate would soon perish and vanish. Why is this?
All those of the two vehicles do not even hear this sutra, much less receive, uphold, read, recite, copy, analyze, or explain it; only the Bodhisattvas are capable of doing so. Therefore—
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, upon hearing this Dharma-gate, should experience great joy and, with a heart of reverence, receive it with respectful veneration upon their heads.
Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who believe in and delight in this sutra will swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O Son of the Buddha, suppose there were a bodhisattva who, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas...
For kalpas, they practice the six pāramitās and cultivate various factors conducive to awakening;

yet, if they have not heard this Dharma-gate of the Tathāgata’s inconceivable and great majestic power, or if, having heard it at some time, they do not believe or understand it, do not follow or enter into it.
They cannot be called true Bodhisattvas, because they are unable to be born into the family of the Tathāgata.
However, if they hear this Dharma-gate of the Tathāgata’s immeasurable, inconceivable, unobstructed, and unhindered wisdom, and having heard it, believe and understand it—

One should know that such a person, by entering into realization in accordance with this, is born into the family of the Tathāgatas, accords with the realm of all Tathāgatas, and is fully endowed with all the dharmas of the bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such merit, they attain unconditioned, spontaneous wisdom with little exertion. It is said in verse:
Such subtle, secret, and profound dharmas are difficult to hear even in hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas;
only those who have been disciplined through diligence and wisdom may hear this secret and esoteric meaning.
If one hears this Dharma and gives rise to joy, they must have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past.
Sustained by the empowerment of the Buddha and revered with constant offerings by gods and humans, this is the supreme wealth that transcends the world;
